tools.name: check_domain
tools.description: Check a domain's SPF (including the 10-DNS-lookup limit), DMARC policy and reporting, DKIM keys on common selectors, and MX records. Returns problems ranked by severity with the fix for each, plus the email services the domain uses.

tools.name: check_sending_ip
tools.description: Check a mail server's IP: reverse DNS (PTR) and whether it resolves back to the IP, and listings on Spamhaus ZEN, Barracuda, SpamCop, PSBL, Mailspike and UCEPROTECT level 1. A refused Spamhaus query is reported as unknown, never as a listing.

tools.name: check_email_headers
tools.description: Check a received email's headers against Gmail's and Yahoo's bulk sender requirements: SPF, DKIM and DMARC results, From domain alignment, one-click unsubscribe (and whether DKIM covers it), TLS, reverse DNS and Message-ID. Use the full headers as the recipient got them (Gmail: Show original).

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_domain, check_email_headers · Private data: check_domain · Public sink: check_domain, check_email_headers.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_domain, check_email_headers · Private data: check_domain · Public sink: check_domain, check_email_headers

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
